newsitem.title: USA: Astra USA wins appeal of EEOC case.
newsitem.headline: Astra USA wins appeal of EEOC case.

text.p: A U.S. appeals court on Friday dismissed part of an injunction against Astra USA prohibiting the company from enforcing settlement agreements with employees who alledged they were victims of sexual harassment.

Astra USA, a unit of Swedish pharmaceutical giant Astra AB, had asked in August the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit to overturn a lower court's ruling, which the company said could open it to lawsuits in connection to allegations of sexual harassment.

Astra entered cash settlement agreements, ranging from $20,000 to $100,000, with at least 11 employees who claimed they were victims of or witnessed sexual harassment, court documents said. The agreements prohibited the employees from filing charges against Astra with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, or helping other employees who wish to file charges.
The EEOC sued Astra and argued in court the provisions of the settlement interferred with three investigations into allegations of sexual harassment at the company and were contrary to public policy.

Astra lawyers said it told its employees they should cooperate with EEOC investigation into allegations of widespread sexual harassment at the company. However, the provision prohibiting employees from filing further charges against Astra allows the company to put the allegations behind and should stand, the Astra lawyers argued.
A U.S. District Court judge in Worcester, Mass. in late June ordered Astra "from entering into or enforcing" both parts of the settlement.

The U.S. Court of Appeals said in court records released on Friday that the settlement does not prevent employees from cooperating with the EEOC investigation, but those who entered into the deal could not file charges.

"The only issue we were concerned about had to do with whether the employees could file new charges. And we were pleased with the decision," said Benjamin Kincannon, a spokesman for Astra. "Having a non-filing provision in settlement agreements is the only way of bringing closure."

"In the facts of this case, the court says we don't need it (the filing provision). We still have a quarrel with these kind of agreements and ultimately I think it is an issue that will be revisited either in this case or another case," said Lou Graziano, trail attorney with the EEOC.

Westborough, Mass.-based Astra USA has been embroiled in a sexual harassment scandel and on June 26 fired its Chief Executive, alleging he engaged in "improper behavior". Astra USA fired one other senior executive and two others resigned.
More than half a dozen former employees filed lawsuits against Astra and its senior executives, arguing that Bildman and others sexually harassed employees and intimidated those who protested.
